main.srt:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,200
 Welcome to the show. Today we are going to talk about

2
00:00:03,200 --> 00:00:06,200
 pricing, and how to decide what to charge.

3
00:00:06,500 --> 00:00:09,600
 I get asked this more than almost anything else,

4
00:00:09,600 --> 00:00:12,200
 so let's take it one step at a time.

5
00:00:12,600 --> 00:00:16,000
 Most people price their work by what feels safe.

6
00:00:16,000 --> 00:00:20,100
 They look at what others charge, they shave a little off,

7
00:00:20,100 --> 00:00:24,100
 and they hope nobody pushes back. But your price is not

8
00:00:24,100 --> 00:00:28,000
 a guess about the market. It is a message about what

9
00:00:28,000 --> 00:00:30,400
 you believe the work is worth.

10
00:00:30,900 --> 00:00:33,700
 Now, I know that sounds nice in theory.

11
00:00:33,700 --> 00:00:36,400
 So let me show you what I actually do.

12
00:00:36,700 --> 00:00:40,700
 Here's the thing about discounts. The moment you offer one,

13
00:00:40,700 --> 00:00:44,300
 you teach people that the first price was never real.

14
00:00:44,300 --> 00:00:48,000
 So start with your costs, add the time it takes,

15
00:00:48,000 --> 00:00:51,600
 add what the result is worth to the person buying,

16
00:00:51,600 --> 00:00:55,800
 and then stand behind that number, and that's why it works.

17
00:00:56,400 --> 00:01:00,200
 That's it for today. If this helped, send it to a friend

18
00:01:00,200 --> 00:01:03,600
 who is stuck on their pricing. See you next time.

suggestions.why: It stands alone: one claim, the reason for it, and the line that ties them together.
suggestions.point: A price is a message about what the work is worth, not a guess about the market.

suggestions.why: It gives the whole method in one breath and ends on its point.
suggestions.point: Do not discount: build the price from costs, time and worth, then stand behind it.

reels.title: Stop discounting your best work
